object_description: two accommodation volumes linked by a lower base
design_condition: The set-back, angled volumes follow the slope through two reference levels and frame a generous southern courtyard while relating selectively to the castle park, village and existing walls.

positive.statement: The two accommodation volumes and lower base create a harmonious informal whole on the historic site.
The building manages the natural slope internally by creating two equivalent reference levels.
The exterior extensions establish a privileged relationship with the village and offer residents safe enjoyment of the courtyard.
The accommodation typology is very compact and rational.
The project shows great accuracy in considering the site, heritage and landscape qualities.
The overall cost benefits from the compactness and simplicity of the volumes.

negative.statement: The ground-floor organization is too schematic and should be reorganized for optimal functioning.
Delivery to the kitchen and logistical flows inside and between the buildings need clarification.
The path toward the east building passes directly in front of rooms and modifies the status of the terrace.
The new constructions pay little attention to existing developments and establish insufficient dialogue with them.
The oversized mineral courtyard damages the landscape and heritage qualities of the privileged southern setting.
The old garden gate appears as a vestige without functionality or connection to the surrounding complex.
The western corner forms a spur toward the old garden wall and contradicts the historically harmonious atmosphere.
The hedged garden rooms introduce an undesirable break with the character of the existing open park.
The park is closed and the relationship between the village and park is not promoted from outside.
The project does not offer adequate solar protection for the generous glazed surfaces.
The buried volume has a strong impact on earth movements.
The accommodation area is slightly above target, although optimization remains possible.
